title: VLAN
what: Logical segmentation of a network using a broadcast domain boundary.
why: To keep traffic separated without physically splitting the network infrastructure.
when: When departments or user groups require logical isolation.
example: Finance and HR networks on the same switch but isolated at Layer 2.
scenarioApplication: A campus or office with multiple departments and different access rules.

title: Inter-VLAN Routing
what: Traffic forwarding between VLANs using a router or Layer 3 switch.
why: To allow controlled communication between segments while preserving isolation.
when: When separate VLANs need a controlled path to a common service or internet access.
example: A student VLAN reaches the internet via a router or L3 switch.
scenarioApplication: Campus or multi-tenant environment with segmentation and routed access.

title: DHCP
why: To reduce manual configuration and support dynamic endpoint growth.
when: When many devices need IPs without static assignment.
example: Wireless clients receive an IP from a DHCP server.
scenarioApplication: A college dorm or office with many transient devices.

title: DNS
what: Name resolution service for human-friendly addresses.
why: To map names to IP addresses for service access.
when: When users need to access services by name or user-friendly endpoints.
scenarioApplication: Campus intranet or enterprise application access.

title: ACL
what: Access control list that permits or denies traffic.
why: To enforce security and policy between segments.
when: When trust boundaries or sensitive services require selective access.
example: Only administrators can reach network management VLAN.
scenarioApplication: Hospital, campus, or branch networks with role-based controls.
